title: The $5B Business Nobody Wants to Build
hook_line: Zapier is worth around five billion dollars for one boring job. Moving data between apps that don't talk to each other.
cliffhanger_line: The solo version of that same job? Pays a reported five hundred to five thousand dollars a month per client. For work most people find too dull to even bother with.
pinned_comment: The full breakdown of who's actually charging this and how — link in bio.
why: Opens on the sharpest number contrast (valuation vs. retainer) and stops right before explaining what the job actually is, forcing viewers to the full video for the mechanics.

title: Why One Person Can Now Do an Integration Team's Job
hook_line: Small companies run on a stack of tools that were never designed to talk to each other.
cliffhanger_line: I automated about eighty percent of that PM busywork with a few AI workflows. And the hours that came back? That was the entire point.
pinned_comment: What those workflows actually looked like, and what to charge for them, is in the full episode.
why: Sets up the problem (disconnected tools) and teases the personal proof point (80% automated) without ever showing the retainer pricing or how to replicate it.

title: The Real Reason Small Businesses Pay for This
hook_line: The pattern looks like this. A one-time build, fifteen hundred to five grand for something simple.
cliffhanger_line: An owner losing three hours a day to copy-paste between systems? They will happily pay a few hundred bucks a month to make those hours disappear. That's the whole pitch.
pinned_comment: The full pricing bands and where the money actually comes from — full video linked.
why: Delivers the pricing numbers as a hook but ends on the psychological reason clients pay, leaving the audience wanting the full evidence stack (Zapier, n8n, market size) that comes right after.

title: The One AI Node That Changes the Pricing
hook_line: A Claude or GPT call inside the workflow can read a messy email, pull the order out of it, and drop clean data into the next system.
cliffhanger_line: And that one node? That's what turns simple automation into something worth an actual retainer.
pinned_comment: The exact stack, cost, and where this node fits — full breakdown in the video.
why: Isolates the single most interesting technical detail (AI-in-the-workflow) as a complete-feeling but unresolved claim, no cost or setup shown, driving to long-form for the actual stack.
